attempts.validity: blockers COMPLETE, other edges 2, pool timeouts 101

report.summary: Transfer failures and slowness coincide with a config change at 15:34:46 that shrank the DB pool from 10 to 2 with a 250 ms timeout. An idle-in-transaction session also blocked others. The outbox is healthy.

findings.claim: A restart at 15:34:46 cut poolMaximumSize from 10 to 2 and connection timeout from 30000 ms to 250 ms.
findings.reason: Runtime config shows the changed settings after the in-window restart.

findings.claim: The pool had 101 acquisition timeouts. This likely explains the 500/503 responses (24% server errors) on /v1/transfers.
findings.reason: Timeouts at the 250 ms limit with max 2 connections line up with 40 500s and 71 503s; the exact status mapping was not observed.

findings.claim: An idle-in-transaction session held locks that blocked two ledger_app sessions for up to ~2 s, which may add to the multi-second latency.
findings.reason: Blocking was seen in 20 samples between 15:34:49 and 15:35:43; p95 is 1.6 s and p99 2.4 s.

findings.claim: Outbox delivery is not the cause: all 367 deliveries succeeded in about 71 ms, with no failures and arrivals equal to publications.
findings.reason: Zero failed events and fast consumer timings.

limitations: Counters restarted twice in the window, and the request counts span restarts.
The outbox dip in arrivals (15:35) matches fewer committed transfers. The status-code to cause mapping was not directly observed.
next_checks: Identify the owner and query of the idle-in-transaction session 51647.
Restore poolMaximumSize and timeout, then re-run the transfer load and compare error rates.

alternatives.reason: The blocker session's origin is unknown and blocking was sampled only every 2 s.
alternatives.hypothesis: The idle-in-transaction blocker alone caused the slowness and errors, independent of the pool change.

alternatives.reason: Deliveries are fast and all succeeded.
alternatives.hypothesis: Slow downstream consumer delivery causes the transfer failures.

report.summary: After the 15:34:46 restart the DB pool shrank to 2 connections with a 250 ms timeout. An idle-in-transaction session held locks, blocking pool connections, so transfers hit acquire timeouts (503/500).

findings.claim: Config change at 15:34:46 cut pool max from 10 to 2 and connection timeout from 30000 ms to 250 ms.
findings.reason: Runtime config shows both values changing at the in-window restart.

findings.claim: Pool exhaustion occurred: 101 acquisition timeouts, max acquire 261 ms, active hit the maximum of 2.
findings.reason: Pool metrics show timeouts at the 250 ms limit and saturation of the 2-connection cap.

findings.claim: An idle-in-transaction session blocked two ledger_app sessions (up to ~2 s) from 15:34:49 to 15:35:43. With only 2 connections, blocked ones starved the pool.
findings.reason: Blocking overlaps the small-pool period. Waiting holders pin both connections, so other requests time out in 250 ms.

findings.claim: Transfers show 111 server errors (503×71, 500×40; ratio 0.228) and p95 1.64 s. Outbox arrivals dipped during the same period.
findings.reason: Errors and latency match the pool timeouts. Arrivals fell from 32 to 8-18 per bucket, then recovered.

findings.claim: Outbox delivery is healthy: 367/367 succeeded at ~71 ms, with no failures.
findings.reason: The consumer is not the source of the slowness. Pending and age rose only briefly.

limitations: Blocking is sampled every 2 s. The idle-in-transaction session's origin and query are unknown.
No per-request trace links individual 503s/500s to pool timeouts, and the second counter restart is unexplained.
next_checks: Identify session 51647 (application_name, query, start time) and why it stays idle in transaction.
Restore pool max and timeout to prior values and re-run the load to confirm errors disappear.

alternatives.reason: All deliveries succeeded with ~71 ms latency, mostly consumer auth time.
alternatives.hypothesis: Slow or failing downstream consumer causing delays

alternatives.reason: Counters restarted twice, but the evidence does not separate restart effects from pool effects.
alternatives.hypothesis: Restart itself caused the errors, independent of pool settings
